verdicts.reason: Reproduced with my own read-only probe (both demo books run through aggregateEngineInput → buildCommandObjects → summarizeCommandContext → explainCommandObject): all 11 items return "Ranked first. Reasons: …" in spotlight mode, and DashboardV4.tsx:65 always asks for that mode while :105 always prints "Highest-priority recommended action". The SMB walkthrough shows "· #2 OF 11" under that kicker. The fix is correct and small: an optional third argument on explainCommandObject leaves the other three callers (Slice.tsx, brief-narrative.ts, the tests) untouched, and "Ranked 2 of 11. Reasons: …" under "Recommended action · #2 of 11" states what is ordered and its basis (COPY_STANDARD §26). The existing tests at command-intelligence.test.ts:201-213 keep passing; add the position case as proposed.

The label is not computed from any comparison: scoreRankingConfidence (scoring.ts:234-260) only adds terms for the one item. In my probe the three tied SMB items (score 89, ordered alphabetically) all read "reasonably clear first choice", and enterprise #2 and #3 read "clear first choice". The proposed wording ("based on several / some / few recorded inputs") is not accurate either, and it is the bland kind of copy the owner does not want: the number is mostly constants (base 36, +12 for two links, +6 for the same two links again, +4 when a readiness summary exists, +6 or +10 by kind of item), so a watched account with no signals at all scores 60–64 = "supported" (probe: "Outbound to NoSignals Inc" conf 60), and with the readiness summary present no aggregator-built card can fall below 58, so the third wording would never show. No statement about support or inputs is true for every item. The approved replacement "priority remains stable" is also unsupported (the stability bonus is never active: state.ts:63 passes no previous snapshot).
verdicts.finalProposed: Remove the label from the default cockpit instead of rewording it: delete CONFIDENCE_PLAIN (DashboardV4.tsx:26-31) and the label text plus its dot at :133-134; keep the "Show next recommendation" button and the "Next:" preview. The reasons line directly above already states the evidence. Leave rankingConfidence / rankingConfidenceLabel in the engine and the export untouched (keys). Record the obligation (B1-X-026 / INV-0633) as NO LONGER APPLICABLE once the label is gone. If the owner wants a line in that position, the only statement the code can support without new logic is a tie notice computed in DashboardV4 from the list itself: when ranked[idx+1] has the same score, print "Tied with the next recommendation on score".

verdicts.reason: Reproduced: "Ranked first. Reasons: risk score 100 out of 100 and evaluation." on every deal card and "Ranked first. Reasons: prospect." for a deal with no risk factor. verdicts.reason: Reproduced: an account named Tripadvisor becomes an "Advisor requests" item with the reason "an advisor request can be reviewed", score 97 against 91 for an identical account, and the oldest surface would print "An advisor intro could get this deal moving — ask this week." for it; deals named Darktrace and Drift score 69 against 65 for an identical deal. Carrying the kind explicitly is the correct fix and is backward compatible: `card.family ?? inferMoveFamily(card)` keeps the title-based path for cards without the field, so the existing family test (command-intelligence.test.ts:52-64) still passes, and no test relies on the text-based drift flag. A narrower alternative for the drift part, if the engine's text check should be kept for other callers, is to have the aggregator pass `driftSignal: false` in the deal card's rankingSignals (an explicit value wins in signalBool).

verdicts.reason: Reproduced in both books and present in both older walkthroughs: "The current list includes 3 deals in recovery, 4 moves queued, and 1 system note." while the list holds 5 deals, 5 outreach items and the ICP item. The numbers are the lengths of capped subsets (command-intelligence.ts:410-416: first 3 deals, first 4 others, first 3 ICP/system), "in recovery" is applied to the first five deals whatever their risk class (Deal Workspace counts 4 at elevated risk in the same book), and "moves queued" is the private recommendation label. Counting the full list by kind and naming each kind ("5 open deals to review, 5 accounts to contact, and 1 setup item") is accurate to what is listed and reads naturally. brief-narrative.test.ts:71-80 matches /2 deals/ and must be updated to the new wording ("2 open deals"); that is a wording update, not a weaker assertion.

The three sentences are chosen from the same per-item number as the cockpit label (see DASH-002) and say something about "the ranking" that the number does not measure: the SMB summary reads "The ranking is well-supported by the live signals." while its first three items are tied and in alphabetical order. "Live signals" will also be read as account signals. The proposed rewording has the same weakness as in DASH-002: "based on several / some recorded inputs" is not true for every item (constants put a watched account with no signals in the middle band), the third variant can no longer occur once the readiness summary exists, and the sentence tells the seller nothing they can use.

A search of src, js and supabase shows the only writers of that field are the cloud column and the cloud seed tool; nothing in Deal Workspace writes it to gtmos_deal_workspaces. My probe loads a stored proposal-stage deal with no next step and 40 days of inactivity as recovery_rank 0, ranking with deals only returns "no-candidates", and with the enterprise seed (United Airlines critical, score 160) the result is "Compose outbound for Boeing".
